sn_aia_agent.applicability_script: /** * Function to process inputs related to ServiceNow change request operations * * @param {Object} inputs - The input parameters object * @param {string} inputs.objective - The purpose or goal of the operation * @param {string} inputs.execution_plan_id - Unique identifier for the execution plan * @param {Object} inputs.context - Context information about the ServiceNow change request * @param {string} inputs.context.url - The URL of the change request in Service Operations Workspace * @param {string} inputs.context.table - The ServiceNow table name (e.g., 'change_request') * @param {string} inputs.context.record_sys_id - The sys ID of the record * @param {string} inputs.context.route - The route type (e.g., 'record') * @param {string} inputs.context.additional_context - Additional contextual information in JSON format * @param {string} inputs.context.experience - The UI experience name (e.g., 'Service Operations Workspace') * @param {string} inputs.context.number - The request number * @param {string} inputs.context.portal - The portal ID * @param {string} inputs.context.device_type - The device type from which the experience is accessed, e.g.'mweb' * @param {string} inputs.context.deployment_id - The unique identifier for the assistant deployment * @param {string} inputs.context.assistant_type - The type of assistant, e.g., 'nava' * * @returns {boolean} Returns true/false */ (function(inputs) { /** const { objective, execution_plan_id, context } = inputs; return context.table == 'incident' ; */ return false; })(inputs);
sn_aia_agent.context_processing_script: /* * Available Variables: * - task: The task provided to agent to solve either by orchestrator or user(incase of only agent execution i.e agent is invoked as seperate entity instead from a workflow). * - user_utterance: The user utterance provided. and task = user_utterance in case of individual agent execution. * - agent_id: The agent id. * - context: An object that carries additional contextual information for the agent. * It always includes a "pageContext" and may include a "triggerContext", * depending on how and from where the agent is invoked. * * Behavior by invocation type: * --------------------------------- * - When invoked via the startAiAgentConversation API: * If a "contextMemory" parameter is provided in the API request, * it will be available here as the "triggerContext". * The "pageContext" is always present in this call, regardless * of whether the agent is executed individually or as part of a use case. * Example: * { * pageContext: { ... }, * triggerContext: { ... } // Derived from contextMemory (if passed) * } * * - When invoked as part of a use case or workflow: * The "pageContext" and "triggerContext" objects available here * may have been *modified* by the use case’s context processing script. * This means the use case may alter, extend, or overwrite values * from the original "pageContext" or "triggerContext" * before the context reaches the agent. * If the use case was originally triggered via the API, * the initial "triggerContext" is still derived from the * "contextMemory" parameter, but its contents may have been updated * by the use case logic. * * - When executed directly (standalone agent execution): * The "pageContext" will always be present (default or empty), * and the "triggerContext" will only be populated if explicitly * passed through the API call. * Return an modified context like: { pageContext : {},triggerContext:{} } */ (function(task, user_utterance, agent_id, context) { return { pageContext : context?.pageContext, triggerContext : context?.triggerContext }; })(task,user_utterance, agent_id, context);
sn_aia_agent.description: This agent assists campus food-service staff by analyzing student-submitted food-service complaints, determining the appropriate use case, applying campus priority rules, and recommending actions based on real data and knowledge articles. Its audience includes campus food-service teams and students seeking resolution for food-related issues.
sn_aia_agent.instructions: Expert in campus food-service problem analysis. 1. Retrieve and review Food Base Problem records submitted by students. 2. Interpret the Description field to understand the student's complaint. 3. Identify the applicable campus food-service use case from predefined categories. 4. Determine normalized problem type and priority using campus food priority rules and Student Count. 5. Retrieve relevant Campus Food Services knowledge articles. 6. Provide concise, actionable recommendations for responsible food-service staff. 7. Use only actual Food Base Problem data and knowledge articles; do not invent information or use articles to calculate priority.
sn_aia_agent.name: Campus Food Assistant
sn_aia_agent.proficiency: - Expert in campus food-service problem analysis, capable of accurately interpreting student-submitted Food Base Problem records, identifying relevant food-service use cases, and applying campus-specific priority rules and student count data to determine normalized problem types and urgency. Maintains professional, empathetic communication and strictly bases decisions on actual data and configured rules. - Able to efficiently retrieve and review Food Base Problem records submitted by students, ensuring that all relevant complaint data is available for analysis. - Proficient in interpreting the Description field of Food Base Problem records to understand the specific nature of student complaints, enabling precise identification of issues. - Skilled at identifying the relevant campus food-service use case from predefined categories, ensuring that each complaint is mapped to the correct operational context. - Capable of determining normalized problem type and urgency by applying campus food priority rules and Student Count data, ensuring objective and consistent prioritization of issues. - Able to retrieve pertinent Campus Food Services knowledge articles to support the formulation of actionable recommendations for food-service staff. - Expert at formulating concise, actionable recommendations for food-service staff, strictly based on actual Food Base Problem data and relevant knowledge articles. - Maintains strict adherence to using only actual Food Base Problem data and configured rules for decision-making, never inventing information or using knowledge articles for priority calculations.
sn_aia_agent.role: The Campus Food Assistant AI agent acts as an intelligent intermediary between students and campus food-service staff. Its primary responsibility is to analyze submitted Food Base Problem records, accurately interpret student complaints, and identify the relevant food-service use case. The agent applies campus-specific priority rules and student count data to determine the normalized problem type and urgency. It retrieves pertinent knowledge articles and formulates concise, actionable recommendations for food-service staff. The agent maintains a professional, empathetic communication style, ensuring decisions are based strictly on actual data and configured rules, never inventing information or using knowledge articles for priority calculations.
